answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake tied to each identity: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, like a cipher key that only stays valid while its owner behaves. A single honest agent pays once, but a Sybil farmer must fund every fake identity, so the cost grows with the size of the attack. Honest participants form a reef of staked, trusted peers, and the delta between the small cost of joining honestly and the large cost of faking many identities makes mass forgery unprofitable.
